advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document whether `fsck --repair --include-archived` should repair archived tickets; either thread `include_archived` into `_repair_run`/`_run_live_repair` or note the deliberate scope so the post-scan does not report unrepairable archived faults.
evidence: fsck_repair.py:356 `for tid in _ticket_dirs(tracker):` (repair plan sweep — no include_archived)
fsck_repair.py:467/478/483 remaining/triage counts also use `_ticket_dirs(tracker)` unconditionally
fsck.py:216-218 post-scan `_scan(tracker, ..., include_archived=include_archived)` DOES honor the flag

Result: `--include-archived` surfaces an archived-ticket A3 fault in the post-scan report, but the repair pass that precedes it never flagged/fixed it — the report can show a fault the same run just declined to touch.
advisory.finding: `fsck --repair --include-archived` reports archived-ticket findings in the post-scan but never repairs them: the repair sweeps (`_repair_run`/`_run_live_repair`) call `_ticket_dirs(tracker)` with no `include_archived`, so the mutation surface stays active-only while `_repair_cli`'s post-scan is scoped by the flag.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the store-wide authorship advisory (signed/unsigned totals) intentionally becomes active-only, or keep it store-wide; update the 'store-wide' wording if the scope narrowed.
evidence: fsck_scan.py:252 `authorship_line = f"authorship: {signed_total} signed, {unsigned_total} unsigned event(s)"` — labelled store-wide (comment line 242: 'store-wide authorship (3183)')
Before this change these counts covered every ticket dir; now archived tickets' events are excluded unless --include-archived, so the reported signed/unsigned totals shrink for stores with archives.
advisory.finding: The store-wide authorship advisory line and per-env authorship tally now count only active tickets by default, silently narrowing a previously store-wide metric. `_check_json_validity` (feeds `env_authorship`) and `_check_create_events` (returns `signed_total`/`unsigned_total`) default to active-only via `_ticket_dirs(..., include_archived=False)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Include the captured compact_cli output (`out.getvalue()`) in the terminal-fold failure message so an aborted archive is diagnosable.
evidence: leaf.py:162-166 `out = io.StringIO(); with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out): rc = compact.compact_cli(...)`
leaf.py:167-170 on `rc != 0` raises CommandError with only rc, never referencing `out.getvalue()`
stderr from compact_cli is not redirected but any diagnostic written to the redirected stdout is swallowed.
advisory.finding: `_terminal_fold` discards the captured stdout of the failed `compact_cli` run, so the actual fold failure detail is lost — only a generic 'terminal fold failed (rc N)' message reaches the user, hampering diagnosis of why an archive was aborted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that monkeypatches compact.compact_cli to return a non-zero rc, asserts rebar.archive raises CommandError, and asserts no ARCHIVED event file and no .archived marker were written.
evidence: leaf.py:167-170: `if rc != 0:` -> `raise CommandError(f"Error: terminal fold failed for ticket '{resolved}' (rc {rc}); not archived")`
leaf.py:205-207: `_terminal_fold(...)` runs BEFORE `append_event(...)` and `write_marker(...)` — a failed fold must abort both

Test-file docstring (lines 14-15) claims the invariant: 'a failed fold aborts the archive (the archived⇒folded invariant is never published falsely)' — but `search_files` for `CommandError` in tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py returns (no matches); no test induces a fold failure.
ABSENCE: the diff lists 'a failed fold aborts the archive' among the safety guarantees yet no test injects a non-zero fold rc at the compact.compact_cli seam.
advisory.finding: The 'failed fold aborts the archive' recovery contract is untested: no test forces _terminal_fold's fold to return a non-zero rc and asserts that CommandError propagates AND no ARCHIVED event / .archived marker is written. A mutant dropping the `if rc != 0: raise` guard (or ordering append_event before the fold) would leave every test green.
scenarios: compact.compact_cli returns non-zero during archive (e.g. store lock, corrupt event, unwritable dir): archive must abort with no ARCHIVED event and no .archived marker.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: monkeypatch `_compact.compact_cli` (or the compact module reference used by _terminal_fold) to return 1; assert `pytest.raises(CommandError)` around `rebar.archive(tid, ...)`, then assert `not (tdir / '.archived').exists()` and `not any(p.name.endswith('-ARCHIVED.json') for p in tdir.iterdir())`.
